analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 1–818), the complete change-range map and the bounded patch. The visible changes describe automatic inclusion of verified update-prefetched builds in the Autopilot set (patch at head lines 14–16) and additional inventory/download status reporting (head line 781). Documentation alone does not establish a bypass of artifact verification, operator consent, admission limits or serving authorization; no concrete regression is supported here.
Relevant existing contracts include exact-build consent and verification (BASE lines 797–818), preservation of ordinary selection in shadow/waiting modes (lines 13–16), shared memory admission (204–214), model-switch usage settlement and coordinator routing barriers (323–384), and encrypted, account-scoped cache reuse under T-041. These interact with A-004, T-012/T-027, T-016, A-009 and TB-011/T-052/T-053, but their implementations are not supplied in these units. Existing logout, attestation, local endpoint and cache-storage descriptions were also examined; the visible patch does not change their controls.
Integration must reconcile the newly documented automatic set expansion and download reporting with actual consent persistence, verified catalog/hash checks, download bounds and shadow/pause behavior. The changes at head lines 786–787, 821–825 and 1885 are outside the visible patch/source content, so their security implications remain unexamined. This is a documentation-local review, not evidence that the implementation or remaining PR is safe.
